To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the bowing of granites is a phenomenon that is influenced by the grain size and the porosity of the rock; (2) the bowing is more pronounced when the grain size distribution is wider and the porosity is higher; (3) the bowing can be reduced by using a more homogeneous granite, or by using a granite with a finer grain size distribution and a low porosity.
bowing of granitic stones occurs when the rock contains a wide grain size distribution and a high degree of porosity.
bowing is a complex process that is influenced by many factors, such as temperature, grain size, mineral shape, porosity, anisotropy and residual stresses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bowing susceptibility of ornamental granites and the influence of the factors mentioned above.
the influence of the microstructure and fabric of ornamental granites on their bowing susceptibility, which is important in the selection of the material for the manufacture of stone veneers.
the influence of petrography on the bowing of granites and with the identification of the most susceptible materials.

the bowing susceptibility of granites is a complex function of the petrographic features of the rock.
the bowing of granitic stones is a function of the rock fabric and the temperature and humidity conditions of the environment.
the bowing of ornamental granitic rocks is a complex process, and it depends on several factors that are not yet fully understood.

the deformation is more likely to occur in granites with coarse grain size and low to moderate porosity.
